abstract: Heating represents a major share of energy use in Germany, making it a critical sector in the energy transition. District heating systems (DHS) are key to decarbonising heat supply, particularly when integrating renewable energy sources and sector-coupled components. However, exploiting this flexibility requires advanced operational strategies. Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly reinforcement learning (RL), offers a promising approach, but its performance must be validated under realistic operating conditions before deployment. This study presents a structured framework for evaluating AI-driven operational strategies using a physics-based dynamic simulation model of a real German DHS. A detailed digital twin was developed in MATLAB/Simulink using the Simscape toolbox, capturing thermo-hydraulic behaviour of heat pumps, stratified thermal energy storage, electric heating rods, a gas boiler, and the network. The AI model, based on reinforcement learning, determines generation dispatch with the objective of increasing renewable utilisation and reducing fossil backup operation. The simulation model is first validated against measured operation for four characteristic historical weeks, establishing a reliable physical reference. Baseline and AI-controlled operation are then compared under identical boundary conditions. Results show robust AI performance under moderate and warm conditions, while systematic underdelivery occurs during colder and highly dynamic periods, revealing limitations of the simplified training environment. The findings demonstrate that high-fidelity dynamic simulation provides a robust, risk-free environment for pre-deployment validation of AI-based control strategies in sector-coupled DHS.

abstract: Optimizing the startup process of combined-cycle steam turbines poses a complex multi-objective, multivariate challenge. Despite the development of numerous optimization approaches, substantial inconsistencies often emerge due to variations in underlying optimization mechanisms and targeted objectives. To address this gap from a mechanistic perspective, this study developed two improved optimization strategies rooted in fundamentally distinct principles. The first, designated as the Mechanism-Driven Random Forest Adaptive Discrete Global Search (MD-RF-GS), is grounded in physical mechanism modeling and incorporates machine learning algorithms; the second, the Response Surface Methodology (RSM), is based on mathematical approximation techniques. Both approaches are applied to an identical standardized cold-start process to perform comprehensive global multi-objective optimization of the startup phase. A systematic comparative analysis is then conducted to assess the mechanisms and characteristics of the two methods across five critical dimensions: automation level, model interpretability, computational cost and response time, optimization accuracy and objectivity, and applicability scope. This work aims to provide actionable guidance for selecting appropriate startup optimization strategies under varying operating scenarios, and to improve the reliability and accuracy of optimization in practical engineering applications.

Preference-conditioned reinforcement learning for balancing occupant comfort and energy efficiency in adaptive residential HVAC control under changing preferences
abstract: In the context of carbon neutrality, enhancing energy efficiency in residential buildings is pivotal for achieving emission reduction targets. Although improving thermal insulation effectively reduces thermal loads, the performance of Air Source Heat Pumps (ASHPs) often degrades under low-load conditions. While conventional Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) can optimize equipment operation, its reliance on pre-defined and static reward functions makes it difficult to adapt to the dynamic and subjective comfort preferences of occupants. To address this limitation, this study proposes a preference-conditioned DRL framework for adaptive HVAC control and implements a large-language-model-based natural language interface for preference input. The framework translates short occupant feedback into explicit preference constraints, enabling flexible and personalized adjustment of comfort–energy trade-offs. To verify the practical feasibility of the proposed method, a hardware integration platform based on Raspberry Pi was developed and deployed in a real-world residential setting. In the field tests, the proposed system achieved a 21% reduction in daily energy consumption under fixed-preference control and a 14% reduction under time-varying preference control compared with the corresponding baseline methods, while maintaining personalized occupant comfort. These findings highlight the potential of adaptive preference-aware HVAC control for improving residential energy efficiency while supporting personalized comfort requirements.

Attitudes toward climate change to demand-driven energy mitigation: A machine-learning approach
abstract: Promoting mitigation behaviors among the public is a fundamental step in addressing climate change, yet such efforts have achieved uneven success across demographic groups. This paper surveys the literature on the relationship between personal attitudes toward climate change and mitigation behaviors, with a particular focus on demand-side energy consumption reductions. An interpretative framework for understanding the key drivers of and barriers to common mitigation strategies is provided. Applying a machine-learning approach to survey data from 23 European countries to disentangle the relative importance of attitudinal predictors, the analysis finds that perceived personal responsibility for climate change is the single most powerful predictor of energy-conscious behavior. This paper thus offers a useful guide to understanding successful approaches to incentivizing climate-friendly action within this regional context.

abstract: Building energy consumption accounts for up to 40% of global energy use, contributing substantially to greenhouse gas emissions. Although demand-side management (DSM) and intelligent control systems have been extensively studied for residential buildings, smart buildings still face critical challenges due to their complex energy consumption profiles and lack of flexible, multi-energy management frameworks. This paper presents a novel multi-objective coordinated energy management system (EMS) that integrates a preference-aware reinforcement-learning framework to balance energy cost and indoor thermal comfort by dynamically coordinating multiple building systems, including heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC), energy storage systems (ESS), and hydrogen storage tanks (HST). To support day-ahead operation under uncertain renewable generation, the proposed EMS incorporates an AI-based extreme learning machine (ELM) model enhanced by a historical data correlation evaluation (HDCE) method, which improves the accuracy of short-term photovoltaic (PV) generation predictions. Simulation results show that the proposed framework can achieve approximately 13.4% energy cost reduction while maintaining nearly negligible user discomfort. In addition, the integrated PV forecasting module achieves a prediction error of 3.33%, which provides reliable renewable input for the coordinated EMS.

A heat exchanger network retrofit method for non-continuous processes based on reinforcement learning
abstract: Non-continuous industrial processes exhibit irregular operating behaviour, characterised by frequent transitions and poorly defined operating regimes. To facilitate systematic analysis and optimisation, such processes are therefore commonly approximated as a set of representative discrete operating states. This study proposes an integrated reinforcement learning framework for heat exchanger network retrofitting under multiple operation states of non-continuous process. The reinforcement learning framework then optimises exchanger areas and network structure while respecting practical retrofit constraints. Unlike conventional machine learning approaches that rely on surrogate models or direct prediction of optimal designs, the proposed framework embeds learning within the optimisation process to adaptively explore retrofit decisions under non-continuous operation. Compared with traditional deterministic optimisation algorithms that require explicit enumeration of all structural constraints and may become infeasible for complex networks, the reinforcement learning approach employs trial-and-error learning on simplified models with fixed exchanger areas, enabling robust optimisation of the overall retrofit problem. Case study results show that the proposed approach reproduces optimisation trends comparable to those obtained using the full dataset and achieves a reduction in total annual cost, with exchanger reassignment and minor retrofit modifications alone delivering savings of approximately $300,000–500,000 and permitting additional heat exchangers increasing the benefit to over $1,000,000.

abstract: The energy management of Hybrid Wheeled All-Terrain Vehicles (HWATVs) operating in unstructured environments faces significant challenges due to stochastic power demands and the lack of representative standard driving cycles. Existing strategies often fail to balance dynamic performance and fuel economy under such extreme conditions. This study proposes a systematic optimization framework integrating energy flow analysis with adaptive control. First, a high-fidelity powertrain test bench is established using the Design of Experiments (DOE) method to precisely quantify the multi-physical energy loss characteristics of the engine, motors, and battery. Subsequently, a driving cycle reconstruction method based on Principal Component Analysis (PCA), K-means clustering, and Markov chains is developed to extract four typical off-road patterns and synthesize stochastic validation cycles from real-vehicle data. On this basis, the Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) is employed to optimize mode-switching thresholds and battery State of Charge (SOC) maintenance ranges for each identified typical driving cycle. Incorporating these optimized parameter sets, an adaptive Energy Management Strategy (EMS) is established featuring online driving condition recognition to dynamically apply the optimal control logic. Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) validation under typical driving conditions and comprehensive driving cycles demonstrates that, compared to traditional rule-based strategies, the proposed approach exhibits superior robustness in stochastic environments. Specifically, it reduces fuel consumption by 0.99%–7.01% and decreases battery charge/discharge cycling frequency by 2.14%–15.30%. This research elucidates the energy-saving mechanism of coupling high-efficiency engine operation with minimized transmission path losses, providing a theoretical foundation for the efficient control of special vehicles in complex terrains.

abstract: The growing importance of hydrogen and sector coupling increases the complexity of Capacity Expansion Models (CEMs) and underscores the need for time-series aggregation methods that balance accuracy with computational efficiency. While previous studies have focused on developing methods for small-scale power sector CEM, this work compares three traditional clustering approaches with a novel DTW-based method (DTW-VD) in terms of statistical accuracy and applies them in a single-node and a multi-node sector-coupled CEMs with seasonal storage. DTW-VD achieves the highest statistical accuracy and best approximates the full-resolution objective function in the single-node case for up to 125 representative days. In the multi-node model, where the true solution is not available, investment decisions based on DTW-VD achieve the best operational performance in 2050. Overall, using two different models and three different weather years, the findings indicate that the performance of time-series aggregation methods depends on the characteristics of the optimization problem, the underlying dataset, and the chosen temporal resolution. The proposed method performs particularly well in complex systems and when a low number of representative periods is used.

abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has shown promise for residential Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) control, but conventional approaches require target-building data, model construction, and policy training, limiting scalability in newly constructed houses. Although transfer learning reduces this burden, scalable zero-shot RL control that avoids target-building data collection, model calibration, and policy retraining remains insufficiently investigated. This study therefore has two objectives: (1) to develop a Cross-building Trust Region Policy Optimization (TRPO) framework for zero-shot residential air-conditioning control, and (2) to determine whether it can achieve performance comparable to room-specific RL in unseen rooms without retraining. EnergyPlus generated residential rooms with diverse thermal characteristics, and thermal-performance indicators were incorporated into the state space to condition the policy on room-specific responses. A single TRPO policy was trained across these tasks and tested in resistance-capacitance (RC) simulation environments constructed from data for two unseen target rooms; these data were used only for evaluation. For the small-design-load room, Cross-building TRPO reduced energy consumption to 64.57% of the fixed-setpoint baseline while maintaining a 100% comfort ratio. For the large-design-load room, where the baseline operated at a high coefficient of performance (COP), both room-specific TRPO and Cross-building TRPO yielded limited additional improvement. Overall, Cross-building TRPO achieved performance close to room-specific TRPO without target-room retraining, demonstrating the feasibility of building-performance-conditioned zero-shot HVAC control. In practice, pre-trained HVAC controllers could be deployed in newly constructed residential buildings using available thermal-performance information, reducing on-site data collection and policy retraining requirements and supporting large-scale deployment.

abstract: Concentrating solar technologies (CST) have shown a wide potential for power generation at highly-irradiated locations and for thermochemical processes and industrial heat production. In particular, solar power tower (SPT) systems are especially effective for high temperature applications. However, a techno-economical gap in terms of operation and maintenance, flux and meteorological conditions’ monitoring, and plant control still hinders the serial industrial adoption of this energy source. In order to tailor an embedded solution for flux prediction and control, this work presents the simulation-to-reality learning step of an Attention-Gated U-Net (AttU-Net) model especially tailored for flux density prediction. This neural network, previously trained with a purely synthetic dataset, has been re-trained with an experimental dataset composed of 562 samples, which was obtained between May 2025, and July 2025. The training results show solid accuracies above 95%, structural similarity indexes (SSIM) up to 97% and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) metrics over 30 dB, which is consistent with model robustness and accuracy. Inference ability and times were tested with 10 held-out samples, reaching accuracies above 96%, SSIMs above 92%, as well as PSNRs above 30 dB. These results suggest the algorithm’s suitability for future integration within flux density control loops to improve plant operability and safety.

abstract: Behind-the-meter microgrid energy management faces a fundamental temporal discrepancy: real-time control decisions at 15-minute resolution must account for financial penalties consolidated over 30-day billing cycles. Under hybrid tariff structures combining time-of-use charges with monthly peak demand penalties, costs are assessed against the highest 15-minute average power within the billing month, rendering standard short-horizon controllers prone to sub-optimality. This paper proposes a Stochastic Model Predictive Control (SMPC) architecture that resolves this conflict by integrating a discrete historical peak state variable into a receding-horizon Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) formulation, coupling each dispatch decision to the accumulated demand exposure of the active billing cycle. Control actions are restricted to Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) dispatch, excluding load shedding and solar curtailment. Forecast uncertainty for load and photovoltaic generation is quantified via a hybrid probabilistic framework: a conformal-prediction-calibrated XGBoost model produces 90% confidence intervals for load demand, while a four-model numerical weather prediction ensemble bounds solar generation uncertainty. Real-time forecast mismatches are mitigated through asymmetric bias correction and adaptive scenario reweighting. Validated on empirical data from a medium-voltage university campus microgrid as a case study, the proposed SMPC achieves a 12.57% cost reduction relative to the unmanaged baseline. A Perfect Foresight MPC sensitivity analysis isolates the cost of load forecasting uncertainty to 1.21%, confirming that residual sub-optimality is driven primarily by the finite prediction horizon and solar stochasticity rather than load forecast inaccuracy.

Temporally-Conditioned Diffusion Transformer for appliance-level load synthesis in Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring
abstract: Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring (NILM) provides appliance-level energy visibility for intelligent building energy management, but deep NILM models remain constrained by limited appliance-level training data and severe class imbalance from sparse appliance activations. Generative data augmentation can alleviate this bottleneck; however, existing NILM generators mainly reproduce appliance waveform morphology or isolated active-event segments, while often neglecting the temporal usage context needed for realistic continuous appliance sequences. To address this gap, this paper formulates NILM data augmentation as a temporally conditioned continuous load synthesis problem and proposes the Temporally-Conditioned Diffusion Transformer (TC-DiT). TC-DiT integrates a DiT-based diffusion-transformer architecture with decoupled multivariate diffusion, AdaLN-Zero temporal conditioning, and active-event continuity enhancement to generate continuous appliance power trajectories that preserve stochastic power dynamics while aligning activations with calendar-derived temporal context. Evaluations on the UK-DALE dataset show that TC-DiT improves waveform fidelity, temporal alignment, and joint power-temporal consistency compared with Generative Adversarial Network (GAN), Time-series Generative Adversarial Network (TimeGAN), and Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM)-Decoupled. Under a Train-on-Real-plus-Synthetic, Test-on-Real (TRSTR) protocol, selecting the best-performing synthetic injection ratio for each appliance-window setting reduces average Mean Absolute Error (MAE) by 18.8% and increases Matching Rate (MR) by 10.9 percentage points over three independent runs; under a fixed global 100% synthetic injection ratio, TC-DiT still achieves a 15.8% MAE reduction and a 9.2 percentage-point MR gain. These results indicate that time-context-aware synthetic load profiles improve downstream NILM performance in the evaluated UK-DALE cross-house setting under data-scarce and class-imbalanced conditions.

Spatio-temporal characterisation of diurnal renewable generation patterns using functional principal component analysis
abstract: In power systems with high renewable penetration, the spatial allocation of weather-dependent resources directly affects system reliability and operational costs. Since electricity demand follows a diurnal pattern, the daily shape of renewable generation determines its contribution to the residual demand profile. However, existing resource characterisation metrics, based on annual potential and variability, carry no information about the daily generation profile shape. This study presents a statistical methodology for the spatio-temporal characterisation of diurnal renewable generation patterns and the clustering of regions with similar patterns. Functional Principal Component Analysis is applied to daily generation profiles to extract the dominant diurnal modes shared across a region, with scores quantifying the expression of each mode per location and day. Feature-based K-means clustering of the mean scores at each location then delineates regions of similar diurnal behaviour. Results are presented for an hourly wind power dataset comprising 10 850 locations in the Western Cape supply region of South Africa over five years. Four components account for 86.2% of the variation about the mean daily profile. The dominant diurnal modes reveal pronounced differences, not captured by annual resource metrics, in the diurnal generation of locations with comparable energy yield, most notably during the evening peak-demand period. The clustering delineates spatially coherent regions of similar diurnal generation behaviour. The proposed approach enables energy planners to characterise diurnal generation patterns across a region in an interpretable, compact form and to identify regions that serve as inputs to long-term planning models.

Interpretable Machine Learning for Predicting Tar and Gas Distributions During Coal Pyrolysis and Exploring Structure–Product Relationships
abstract: A framework coupling reactive molecular dynamics (ReaxFF MD) with interpretable machine learning was developed to relate coal molecular structure to pyrolysis product distributions. Pyrolysis simulations of 161 coal macromolecular models spanning different ranks were conducted under consistent conditions. Feature selection, model comparison, and cross-validation yielded separate models for semicoke, light tar, heavy tar, pyrolysis gas, and pyrolysis water mass fractions. Within this simulation dataset, gradient boosting regression (GBR), partial least squares regression (PLS), and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) performed best for semicoke, pyrolysis gas, and heavy tar, respectively, with test-set R2 values of 0.9920, 0.9977, and 0.8909. The light tar XGBoost and pyrolysis water random forest (RF) models achieved test-set R2 values of 0.6295 and 0.6214. Their relatively limited predictive ability may reflect limited sample size and difficulty capturing secondary reactions and dynamic structural evolution using initial static descriptors. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analysis ranked O-linked methylene and the H/C ratio highest by mean |SHAP| in the heavy tar and pyrolysis gas models, respectively. Accumulated local effects (ALE) and individual conditional expectation (ICE) analyses indicated generally positive associations between counts of O-linked methylene and ether bridges and predicted heavy tar mass fractions. Heavy tar model responses to the O/C and H/C ratios varied across ranges and samples. Pyrolysis gas predictions generally responded positively to the H/C ratio, degree of aromatic substitution, and Num naphthenic rings. This framework predicts product distributions and interprets structure–product relationships within a specified ReaxFF MD system, informing coal structure screening and targeted product control.
